ai.definition: Reasoning-Agentic Workflows are AI systems designed to tackle complex, open-ended tasks through iterative loops of planning, execution, and reflection. These workflows incorporate Chain-of-Thought (CoT) reasoning to generate step-by-step explanations for their actions and ReAct frameworks to self-correct and utilize external tools.
ai.howItWorks: These systems start with a problem statement or task, break it down into smaller steps using CoT, execute these steps in the real world, collect feedback, analyze outcomes, and refine their approach through reflection. This process allows them to improve over time without explicit human intervention.
ai.problemSolved: Challenges associated with complex decision-making processes that require multiple steps of reasoning and external tool usage, such as software development or strategic planning tasks where traditional rule-based systems fall short.
ai.manufacturing: The manufacturing process involves developing the AI models, integrating them into workflows, testing in controlled environments, and then deploying to real-world scenarios. This includes training data collection, model tuning, and integration with existing infrastructure.
ai.buildProcess: Builds on existing machine learning techniques but introduces more sophisticated methods like CoT and ReAct. The process involves iterative development cycles where the AI system is tested against a variety of tasks, receiving feedback to improve its performance.
ai.costDrivers: High initial investment in data collection and model training, ongoing costs for maintenance and updates, and potential costs associated with tool integration and infrastructure upgrades.
ai.lifecycleOutlook: Growing adoption but still in the early stages of widespread implementation across industries.
ai.regulation: Regulatory frameworks are emerging but not yet standardized. Issues around data privacy, transparency, and accountability will need to be addressed as these systems become more prevalent.
ai.risks: Risk of bias in training data leading to skewed outcomes, potential misuse of tools, and the complexity of maintaining and updating AI models over time.
ai.profitability: Potential for significant cost savings and efficiency gains in complex decision-making processes, but profitability depends on specific use cases and industry contexts.
ai.futureDevelopment: Future development will likely focus on improving explainability, reducing bias, enhancing tool integration capabilities, and expanding the range of tasks these workflows can handle.
ai.energyRequirements: Field units draw low hundreds of watts; fabrication is energy-intensive due to vacuum baking. Overall operational power consumption varies based on task complexity but remains relatively low compared to human labor in many scenarios.

glossary.def: A reasoning technique where AI systems explain their thought process step-by-step, making them more transparent and easier to debug.
Approaches that enable AI agents to use external tools and continuously adapt based on feedback from the environment or human users.

subsystems.name: Reasoning engine
subsystems.role: the language model that produces plans, thoughts and tool calls.

subsystems.name: Planner
subsystems.role: breaks an open-ended goal into ordered, checkable steps.

subsystems.name: Tool interface
subsystems.role: lets the agent act on the outside world.

subsystems.name: Memory and retrieval
subsystems.role: keeps context and past experience available across steps.

subsystems.name: Reflection and critic
subsystems.role: checks intermediate and final results, then triggers corrections.

subsystems.name: Orchestration loop
subsystems.role: runs the plan-act-observe-reflect cycle and manages retries.

subsystems.name: Guardrails and oversight
subsystems.role: keeps actions bounded, auditable and safe.

buildSteps.title: Define the task and success metric
buildSteps.detail: Pick a bounded open-ended task, such as fixing a bug or answering a multi-source question, and write down what a correct result looks like.

buildSteps.title: Select and prompt the base model
buildSteps.detail: Choose a model with strong reasoning and tool-use ability, then write a system prompt that explains the loop and the available tools.

buildSteps.title: Expose tools with strict schemas
buildSteps.detail: Wrap search, APIs and code execution as functions with typed arguments and clear descriptions so the model can call them reliably.

buildSteps.title: Implement the control loop
buildSteps.detail: Code the cycle: the model proposes a thought and an action, the action runs, the observation is fed back, and the loop repeats until a stop condition is met.

buildSteps.title: Add memory and retrieval
buildSteps.detail: Store the running transcript, summarise old steps to save context, and retrieve relevant documents or past successes when needed.

buildSteps.title: Insert reflection and verification
buildSteps.detail: After key steps, ask the model or a separate critic to check the result, and run tests or validators wherever the task allows.

buildSteps.title: Set budgets and guardrails
buildSteps.detail: Cap steps, tokens, time and cost; run code in a sandbox; require human approval before irreversible or high-impact actions.

buildSteps.title: Build an evaluation harness
buildSteps.detail: Run the agent on a held-out set of tasks, measure success, and inspect traces to find where planning or tool use failed.

buildSteps.title: Deploy with monitoring
buildSteps.detail: Log every action, watch for drift or repeated failures, and keep an operator able to intervene or roll back.

prerequisites.tech: Large language models with reasoning ability
prerequisites.why: they generate plans, code and critiques, though reliability varies with task complexity.
they let a model invoke external functions in a structured, repeatable way.
they supply relevant context beyond what the model learned in training.
context windows have grown, but agents still lose coherence over many steps.
there is no general method to prove an agent will obey safety constraints in all situations.

prerequisites.tech: Standard evaluation benchmarks for open-ended tasks
prerequisites.why: existing tests cover narrow skills, not the messy multi-step work agents are meant to do.

pathway.milestone: single-agent workflows that plan, call tools and reflect under human supervision
pathway.unlocks: automation of coding, research and data tasks with a person checking key outputs.

pathway.milestone: multi-agent systems with specialised roles and shared memory
pathway.unlocks: larger projects handled by decomposition and parallel work.

pathway.milestone: standardised tool and identity protocols across services
pathway.unlocks: agents that can safely use many external systems without custom integration each time.

pathway.milestone: reliable long-horizon autonomy with formal guardrails
pathway.unlocks: delegation of end-to-end business processes and scientific workflows.
